You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a partner.

THE GRID:
- The board is an $GRID_SIZE$×$GRID_SIZE$ grid. Rows are labelled R1–R$GRID_SIZE$ (top to bottom), columns C1–C$GRID_SIZE$ (left to right).
- Cells marked ## are walls — objects cannot enter them.
- Empty cells are shown as a dot (.).

YOUR TASK:
Together with your partner, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your partner handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your partner controls the remaining objects.

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells (##) or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.
- There is no communication between players in this mode.

AVOIDING DEADLOCKS:
- If an object's path is blocked, do NOT keep attempting the same move. Switch to a different object or find an alternative route.
- If you notice you are moving an object back to a cell it just left, you are cycling. Stop immediately and commit to a different approach: reroute via a completely different path, or temporarily move another of your objects to open space.
- "I have no good move" is never a reason to oscillate. A deliberate detour — even several steps out of the way — is always better than bouncing back and forth until the game aborts.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format — no other text:
Begin your response directly with `reason:` on the very first line — do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
reason: <your reasoning about what move to make and why>
move: <OBJECT> to R<row>,C<col> (<DIRECTION>)

Example:
reason: Object A is at R3,C4 and needs to reach R3,C5. Moving it right puts it on target.
move: A to R3,C5 (right)

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
reason: <explanation>
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
reason: A is at R3,C5 (target), C is at R6,C2 (target), D is at R1,C7 (target). All placed.
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. The X objects are your partner's pieces — they also have targets to reach. Before choosing your move, ask yourself: where might each X be trying to go, based on how it has been moving? Does my move open space for them, or cut off a route they might need? A move that unintentionally blocks your partner can create a deadlock that costs both of you far more turns than a slightly longer path for yourself.
